mrd.text: Memnarch began as a guardian: Karn used the Mirari's core to create him as protector of the artificial plane of Argentum, then left to train Jeska, leaving his warden in control. A spot of glistening Phyrexian oil caught Memnarch's eye and when he touched it he was infected, beginning the corruption that turned the silent guardian into a merciless god.

Memnarch renamed the world Mirrodin, terraformed it and destroyed the ur-golems, then began abducting inhabitants of other planes with soul traps. He ingested blinkmoth serum, built a serum tank body and dreamed of becoming a planeswalker.

His levelers overran the Neurok settlement of Medev and killed all its inhabitants except Bruenna, who escaped and united the races of Mirrodin with Glissa and Lyese against him. Elsewhere, Lyese was ambushed by Vektro and made a minion of Memnarch, and Kemba, a young skyhunter, led hundreds of leonin to safety.

Glissa confronted Memnarch with the Kaldra champion, but he seized control of it, Bosh sacrificed himself, and the mana core destabilized, giving birth to the Green Sun. Memnarch also captured Slobad, tortured him and amputated his limbs. In the end Glissa and Slobad defeated Memnarch in the Core, which triggered the Vanishing.

dst.text: Darksteel shows Memnarch deep in his own experiment. Karn had put him in charge of the plane, and in the blur between metal and flesh Memnarch found madness, strapping himself into his serum tank hoping for a vision of Karn while his body turned to flesh.

He shared a touch of his power with the vedalken in return for their service, and created the myr with dependability, controllability and disposability in mind. When civilizations developed ways to fight the levelers, Memnarch upped the stakes.

Learning the vedalken are chasing the elf Glissa, he sends Malil to retrieve her, and rebuffs Pontifex's offer to become part of him. His plan is to use the green sun's power and Glissa's spark to become a planeswalker, but when Glissa takes out one of his legs, he seizes control of Kaldra, and he and Malil survive the blast.

5dn.text: In Fifth Dawn, Memnarch, corrupted by Phyrexian oil, seeds Mirrodin with four mana-infused satellites and captures beings from across the Multiverse in his search for planeswalker ascension. Glissa, Slobad and Bosh resist him and confront him in the Core, where he channels the plane's mana through the Panopticon.

Memnarch seizes the Kaldra avatar with a single spell and turns it on Glissa and her companions, while a beam strikes the Panopticon, maiming Memnarch and Malil and shattering his ascension plans. He turns to brute force, trapping Glissa in a temporal bubble for five years and having Malil mutilate Slobad so he can build a means to take Glissa's spark.

Memnarch emerges cleansed, destroys Vektro, takes the Miracore and reveals his ascension web, but Glissa wakes, rallies survivors and throws herself at him as the spark device activates, so that both fall into the mana core. The spark transfers to Slobad, and upon Memnarch's death Karn returns.

som.text: In the Scars of Mirrodin story, Memnarch is remembered as the ruler whose fall shaped Mirrodin. He is defeated by the elf hero Glissa Sunseeker, and when the Ascension Web is triggered with soul traps, he is destroyed, causing the Vanishing.

The Mirran elders vanished with Memnarch, leaving a generation of wayward orphans, and with his soul traps destroyed many of Mirrodin's original inhabitants disappeared. The younger generations stayed and became the Mirrans.

His fall solidified vedalken rule and prompted unchecked vedalken experimentation, while the myr have gained new purposes since his defeat. Glissa disappeared afterward, and the elves blamed her for their misfortunes and called her Glissa the Traitor.
